messages:
support-bot: New ticket #9127 opened by big-retailer — intermittent 502/504s from hosted inference (us-central1) since 12:14 UTC. Customer link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/9127.

nina: jumping in. They reported 502 with payload: {\"error\":\"control_plane_failure\",\"detail\":\"routing-service: unable to fetch policy: read timeout\",\"code\":502}. They also included a few request IDs.

karim: thanks. Which control-plane component returned the 502? routing-policy or auth?

support-bot: trace for req_id=req_0a1b2c: request routed to control-plane-rp-1 -> routing-policy-service -> attempted DB read from configdb-replica-2 -> timeout -> returned error to gateway.

ops-oncall: checking k8s and infra metrics: routing-policy pods show p95 latency spike at ~12:12. CPU/memory steady. Postgres replica cluster shows increased replication lag and occasional connection errors to replica-2.

db-admin: I see network error logs on replica-2 around 12:11-12:16 UTC: "connection reset by peer" from internal network fabric. Primary still healthy. Replica-2 accepted fewer connections and had queries queued -> client timeouts.

karim: so routing-policy tried reading routing configs and hit replica-> timed out. Shouldn't we prefer primary for critical reads? Is replica used for routing lookups?

ops-oncall: routing-policy read preference is read-any, replicas used to scale reads. Under normal load it's fine, but when replica lag or transient network issues occur, queries can take >2s and our client times out at 1s, causing route resolution errors.

nina: customer impact: they saw ~12% error rate for 10 minutes, p50 latency doubled then many 504s. They're asking for root cause and mitigation.

karim: immediate mitigations: 1) pin routing-policy to primary-only reads temporarily, 2) bump DB client timeout to 3s, 3) fail open to cached route if DB cannot be reached (serve with possible stale route), 4) rollback recent routing-policy config changes if any. Which is fastest?

ops-oncall: fastest is to change read preference to primary-only in us-central1 cluster for routing-policy via config map; applying config doesn't require deploy. Doing that now as canary.

deploy-bot: configmap updated for routing-policy-service in us-central1 by ops-oncall at 2026-03-22T12:24:30Z.

ops-oncall: applied change. Monitoring connection count and errors.

ops-oncall: post-change: replica-2 errors drop, routing-policy p95 latency back to normal, control-plane 502 rate decreased to near zero within 90s.

nina: emailed customer: "We've temporarily switched routing-policy to read from primary only in us-central1 to avoid replica timeouts. We're investigating the replica network errors and will follow up with permanent fix. Please let us know if you still see failures."

db-admin: investigating replica-2: host shows NIC flapping messages in kernel log tied to host vm kernel upgrade earlier today (host maintenance window at 11:50). Looks like kernel upgrade triggered transient interface resets during boot sequence after auto-update. We'll schedule a controlled reboot and move replica to another node.

karim: engineering follow-ups: - add DB client fallback to primary if replica query fails with timeout - add route-cache fallback to control-plane so routing-policy can respond with cached entry (stale-ok) rather than propagate 502 - create alert: replica_io_errors > 5/min -> page DB-admin - tune client timeout and exponential backoff for read-any strategy

sre-jen: I'll file an incident with timeline + customer affected list. Severity: high, impacted hosted inference in us-central1.

nina: any immediate risk of cascading errors to other regions?

ops-oncall: no signs of same issue in us-west1/us-east1. Replica issue isolated to one host in us-central1. We will cordon the host and reschedule replica.

db-admin: cordoned host and rescheduled replica to node-17 at 12:39 UTC. Rebuild/replay completed and replica lag normalized.

karim: after replica moved, we can revert routing-policy to read-any but let's keep the primary-only change for 10m additional margin, then revert gradually. Also prepare a small patch to the DB client to add explicit host failover preference and increased timeouts for short-lived reads.

nina: customer confirmation: "We reran our integration tests and errors are gone. Thanks for the quick fix." :tada:

ops-oncall: rolling back read-preference to read-any at 12:50 UTC with canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Watching metrics now.

deploy-bot: configmap reverted in us-central1 by ops-oncall at 2026-03-22T12:50:45Z. Canary progression healthy.

karim: post-incident items: PR to add cached-route fallback + metrics for cache hit/miss, add unit tests simulating replica timeout, update runbook to prefer primary for control-plane route reads during DB infra maintenance, update alert thresholds.

nina: closing loop with customer and documenting changes in ticket #9127. Assigning follow-ups to karim and db-admin.

support-bot: ticket #9127 marked mitigated.

sre-jen: I'll create the postmortem doc and link the logs, configmap diff, and the host maintenance note.

karim: note for postmortem: reproduction script (simulates replica network drop):
```bash
# simulate replica timeout by blocking traffic to replica IP
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.2.3.45 -j DROP
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/resolve -d '{"tenant":"x"}' & done
sleep 3
iptables -D OUTPUT -d 10.2.3.45 -j DROP
```
karim: thanks all. We'll close once PRs and runbook updates are merged."
